Scale meal assembly with robots built for the real world. Customers have seen: 2-3x output 88%↓ giveaway 60%↑ labor productivity 30%↑ consistency Request a demo Trusted by the top companies in the industry Building the infrastructure for domestic production America doesn't have a shortage of demand for food. It has a shortage of people available to produce it. Physical AI can give food manufacturers the productive capacity to grow domestically rather than sending production elsewhere. 1.137 M unfilled jobs in US food manufacturing 3.1 M unfilled jobs by 2030 300 % annual staff turnover rate Traditional automation wasn’t built for the complexity of food ‍ Many of our customers have tried traditional automation (multi-head dispensers, vibratory feeders, and volumetric fill dispensers) before turning to Chef. These systems struggle with the natural variability of food ingredients, frequent changeovers, and high-mix production, leaving companies no choice but to rely on manual labor. We believe this work shouldn’t have to be done by hand. Physical AI makes robots intelligent enough to handle food ChefOS, our physical AI operating system, enables Chef robots to manipulate real food in all its natural variability. Mixed veggies Pulled meat Leafy greens Discrete items Drag the image and select different ingredients Learn more about ChefOS Chef’s AI-enabled robots are as flexible as workers Learn more about Chef robots Our meal assembly robots work with: Your ingredients Your portion sizes Your trays, burritos, wraps, and pizza bases Your placement styles Your conveyors Chef’s robotic module C-001748 is NSF-certified Chef’s robotic module C-001748 is certified under “NSF/ANSI 169 – Special Purpose Food Equipment and Devices,” a standard for commercial food equipment. This certification confirms that the robot meets strict requirements for food safety and cleanability. Robots in production Chef robots are deployed at more than a dozen customer facilities across the US, Canada, and Europe. 98,578,982 servings in production Meet our customers CASE STUDIES Project Open Hand The San Francisco-based nonprofit uses Chef robots powered by physical AI to address staff shortages and deliver consistent, medically tailored meals to people in need.
